q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most, and their audiences are mildly positive. Among small channels, 35.6% of videos with a baseline outperformed (n=90 of 112 videos). Their mean relative lift was 9.3, and net sentiment was +6 (39.3% positive, 33.4% negative, n=2,740 product-side comments).

Mid channels: 22.0% outperformed (n=50 with baseline, 51 videos), mean lift 4.6. They have the happiest audiences, at net +11 (41.6% positive, 30.9% negative, n=2,332).

Large channels: only 5.4% outperformed (n=37 with baseline, 50 videos), mean lift 1.8. Sentiment is slightly negative at net -2 (36.3% positive, 38.6% negative, n=1,932).

Caveat: the sample is comments only, and these are associations, not causes. Large and mid group video counts are modest.
sql:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer
  FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id
  WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
lift AS (
  SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(outperformer IS NOT NULL) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS mean_rel_lift
  FROM v WHERE size_group IS NOT NULL GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
  SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
    ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pos_share,
    ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS neg_share,
    ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment
  FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id
  WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND v.size_group IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT l.size_group, l.n_videos, l.n_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.mean_rel_lift, s.n_product_side, s.pos_share, s.neg_share,
  CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=l.size_group
ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions look like the most dependable format for mid-sized channels: 8 of 19 videos (42%) outperformed their baseline, with an average relative lift of 2.9 (n=19). That is the largest sample in the result.

Durability test hit 100% outperformance, but it's a single video (n=1), so it tells us almost nothing. Explainer tips have the highest average relative lift (15.4), yet only 1 of 8 videos outperformed (12.5%), which suggests a single big hit is pulling the average up.

Upgrade advice (n=8) also had a 12.5% outperformer rate, with an average lift of 1.8. Comparison (n=6), meme shorts (n=5, 4 with baseline), keynote recaps (n=2) and other (n=2) had no outperformers.

Caveat: sample sizes are small outside first impressions, and these are associations, not proof that format causes the results.
sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(p.outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.lift),3) AS avg_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' GROUP BY c.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
The two most negative high-lift videos are:

1. "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" has a net sentiment of -58 (12% positive, 69% negative, n=78). Its lift is 499.76, or 116.5x relative lift.
2. "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" has a net sentiment of -53 (18% positive, 70% negative, n=57). Its lift is 86.82, or 20.2x relative lift.

Both are well above typical performance, but lift measures reach and sentiment measures reaction, so a big lift doesn't mean viewers liked the video. Sample sizes are moderate. These figures also come from a sample of comments, not all viewers.
sql: SELECT video_id, title, url, format, ROUND(lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, outperformer, n_product_side, ROUND(pct_positive,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(pct_negative,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(pct_positive - pct_negative,3) AS net_sentiment FROM v_content WHERE topic='duo' AND format!='official' AND outperformer=1 AND n_product_side>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, pct_negative DESC LIMIT 10

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Samsung Did It First is the largest topic (n=1,058, 10.7% of 9,928 comments), followed by Eager to Buy (n=579, 5.8%), Praise for review quality (n=544, 5.5%), Apple ad parody humor (n=479, 4.8%) and Price Complaints (n=478, 4.8%).

The fastest growth, last 7 days vs prior 7, is in smaller topics:
- Left-Handed Concerns: +585% (89 vs 13)
- Waiting for Next Year: +410% (51 vs 10)
- Wanting Pro Cameras: +273% (41 vs 11)
- Apple ad parody humor: +227% (121 vs 37)
- Eager to Buy: +212% (203 vs 65)

Samsung Did It First added the most comments (+191, about +201%), then Eager to Buy (+138).

Caveat: the top-growth topics start from small bases (prior n of 10 to 13), so their percentages can swing easily. Several topics with prior n under 10 show no growth figure.
sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official'), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM sc), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS t FROM sc), agg AS (SELECT sc.topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN sc.d > mx.m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_last7, SUM(CASE WHEN sc.d <= mx.m-7 AND sc.d > mx.m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev7 FROM sc, mx WHERE sc.topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sc.topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/tot.t,3) AS share_of_all_comments, tot.t AS n_all_comments, a.n_last7, a.n_prev7, CASE WHEN a.n_prev7>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(a.n_last7-a.n_prev7)/a.n_prev7,3) END AS wow_growth, (a.n_last7-a.n_prev7) AS abs_change, mx.m AS latest_day FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot, mx ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo sits second of six topics, with a net sentiment of +5 (39% positive, 34% negative; n=7,004 comments across 190 videos).

- iPhone 18 Pro is higher at +12 (39% positive, 27% negative; n=3,591). Its positive share matches Duo's, but it draws fewer negative comments.
- The other topics are all net negative: competitor foldables -3 (n=479), other -2 (n=240), general event videos -8 (n=1,484).
- iPhone 18 is the lowest at -36 (60% negative), but n=169 across 6 videos is small, so treat it cautiously.

Caveat: these are comment samples, not all viewers, and the "other" topic is also small (7 videos).
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic HAVING COUNT(*)>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Commenters like the buying appetite and the favourable comparisons with Samsung's foldables, and they criticise the price, durability worries and the under-display camera.

Liked most:
- Eager to Buy: net +22 (45% positive, 22% negative, n=579).
- Samsung Fold Comparisons: net +15 (47% positive, 32% negative, n=442).
- Positive Video Reactions: net +40, but n=158 is small.

Criticised most:
- Under-Display Camera: net -17 (24% positive, 41% negative, n=300), the weakest score.
- Price Complaints: net -6 (n=478).
- Folding Phone Durability Doubts: net -2 (n=453).

The biggest topic, "Samsung Did It First" (n=1,058), is split evenly at net +1, with 40% positive and 39% negative.

Caveat: these are comment-sample topics, and a comment can touch more than one, so treat the groups as overlapping.
sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND cm.topic_id IS NOT NULL), agg AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(c.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(c.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='positive')/COUNT(*),3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='negative')/COUNT(*),3) AS neg_share FROM c JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE t.pool='product' GROUP BY t.topic_id, t.name), liked AS (SELECT 'most_liked' AS list, * FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8), crit AS (SELECT 'most_criticised' AS list, * FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8) SELECT * FROM liked UNION ALL SELECT * FROM crit LIMIT 40
